_comment: Migration step for the plugin protocol jump P8 -> P9. Consumed by `mads plugin --update`. P9 adds the shared-memory (zero-copy) blob API -- BlobView/BlobBuffer, Source::supports_shared_output()/get_output_shared(), Filter::load_data_view()/supports_shared_output()/process_shared(), Sink::load_data_view() -- as virtual methods whose defaults copy, so no plugin source changes are needed: the mads_plugin pin moves, the Release build-type default moves before project() (see the replacement below), and the plugin is recompiled. See src/main/plugin_migrate.hpp for the transform semantics.

replacements._comment: Up to P8 the template defaulted CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE to Release *after* project(), where MSVC with a single-config generator (Ninja, NMake) has already set it to Debug: such plugins were built Debug against a Release MADS. Captures the project() line ($1) and the old if(...) block after it, and puts the new default first. Does not match again once applied.
replacements.description: Default the build type to Release before project() (MSVC otherwise builds Debug)
replacements.replacement:
# Release by default. This must come before project(): there, single-config
# generators with MSVC already initialize CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE to Debug, and a
# Debug plugin cannot share std::string/json objects with a Release MADS
# (different C runtimes).
if(NOT DEFINED CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE AND NOT DEFINED CMAKE_CONFIGURATION_TYPES)
  set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE "Release" CACHE STRING "Choose the type of build.")
endif()
$1

notes: No source changes are required: P9 only adds virtual methods with copying defaults. Rebuild the plugin against mads_plugin v2.6-P9 and it keeps working as before; incoming blobs reach load_data() through the default load_data_view(), which makes one copy.

CMakeLists.txt: the Release build-type default now comes before project(). On Windows, MSVC with a single-config generator (e.g. Ninja) initialized the build type to Debug first, so plugins were built Debug against a Release MADS, which uses a different C runtime. If your CMakeLists.txt sets the build type differently, check that a plain `cmake -Bbuild` on Windows now builds Release.

Zero-copy input (filters and sinks) is opt-in: override load_data_view(Tin const &data, std::string topic, BlobView blob) and read blob.data in place. The view is read-only and valid only for that call (for filters, through the following process()); copy anything you need to keep. The host re-checks the shared-memory slot after the call and drops torn reads.

Zero-copy output (sources and filters) is opt-in: return true from supports_shared_output() and implement get_output_shared(out, buf) / process_shared(out, buf), writing at most buf.capacity bytes into buf.data and setting buf.size. If the blob does not fit, set buf.size to the required size and return return_type::retry: the host falls back to get_output()/process() in the same loop iteration.
Shared output is only used when the agent runs with `shm = true` in its settings section, and only for consumers on the same host; see `man mads-source` and the shared-memory guide.
If you have heavily customized CMakeLists.txt, compare it with that of a freshly generated plugin (e.g., using `git diff` or a file comparison tool).
